mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% month-over-month, signals supply-side stress that elevates input costs and depresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS MoM < -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) and housing starts (HOUST > 1% monthly growth) for two consecutive months signals strengthening demand fundamentals, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM > 0.5% AND HOUST MoM > 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and real retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% signals broad-based demand and supply weakness, which should persistently depress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.
